title: A finer broadcast whose first copy is at the hour's last receipt sets the hour box, and is precise through a copy one second later
reasoning: ADR 0003 at bfe51aa records Casey's answer (issue #55 comment 6995037213, item 3): "A broadcast's gateway copies count as one position, timed by the first copy, precise if any copy qualifies." Its late-edge sentence: "At a window's late edge, a first copy just inside means the broadcast is read and counts as precise even when its only qualifying copy arrived just outside. The late edge is ... the last of the link-hour's receipts with a position at both ends for the hour box".

c54-r's broadcast, packet 54003, cell c20 at 20 bits, reached c54-h1 on the public broker at 23 10:30:00 (c54-m003) and c54-h2 on MeshSTL only at 10:30:01 (c54-m004). The copies share node, packet id and stored values, so they are one position, timed 10:30:00, and it qualifies under pos_04 through c54-m004 (20 bits, seen_meshstl true). The copies' gateways are not c54-g and the rows have no relay_node, so they are no receipts and make no candidate at c54-g.

c54-r's only other position is a 16-bit cell K on the public broker at 22 09:05 (c54-m002: stored 385974272, -903643136; edges 385941504 to 386007040 and -903675904 to -903610368). K holds the broadcast's stored value 386000896, -903657472, so the two cells overlap and are the same place, and K is the coarser.

The receipts are at 10:10, 10:20 and 10:30, and all three have a position at both ends, so 10:30 is the last of them. At 10:10 and 10:20 c54-r is stationary on K alone. At 10:30 its look-back holds K and the broadcast, timed at the receipt's own instant (c46), and it is stationary on c20, K being set aside as a cell that holds a finer position (lnk_02, D3').

Step 6: c54-r is stationary at every receipt, and the union from 16 10:10 (7 days before the first receipt) to 23 10:30 (the last) holds K and the broadcast, which are the same place. Its hour box is chosen from that union: K holds the finer c20 and is set aside, so the box is c20, and every receipt uses it (lnk_02: "that union can hold a position sent later in the same hour than a receipt"; c21). c54-g is stationary on its 16-bit position of 22 09:00 at every receipt and on its hour box, g16. One box per end (step 8).
relayer_precise_source reads the union the hour box was chosen from (PLAN, Data model). The box's only cell, c20, was sent in the broadcast, which qualifies through c54-m004, so the flag is true.

Timed by its later copy, the broadcast would be at 10:30:01, outside the union and every look-back: the hour box would be K, every receipt would use K (2854.588743 m to g16) and the flag would be false. Counted copy by copy, c54-m003 at 10:30:00 would be in the union and the box would still be c20, but c54-m004 would be outside it, so the flag would be false.
gateway_precise_source is false: c54-g's only cell has 16 bits and was sent on the public broker.

Every receipt is a direct hop (relay_node 21 is c54-r's own byte, lnk_01) and passes lnk_05 at 2745.603337 m from c20 to g16, boxes not overlapping. The hour has 3 packets: kept. Medians: SNR 5, 6 and 7 dB give 6.0; RSSI -90, -95 and -100 dBm give -95.0. position_uncertainty_m is c20's 22.734410 m plus g16's 363.750397 m, = 386.484807 m (lnk_05).
